details: Bitcoin has recovered towards $84,000, extending its rally from last week's sell-off. This rebound is attributed to an easing of geopolitical tensions, specifically between the US and Iran, and a return to positive inflows in Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), which saw $21 million in net inflows recently, ending a streak of substantial withdrawals. The crypto market had previously faced pressure from fears of sustained inflation and higher US interest rates. Despite the recovery, Bitcoin remains sensitive to macroeconomic factors.
title: Bitcoin Rebounds as Geopolitical Tensions Cool and ETF Outflows Ease

details: Bitcoin is trading near $84,000, maintaining its weekend recovery even with significant withdrawals from US spot Bitcoin ETFs, which recorded $681 million in net outflows last week—the largest weekly total since June. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined 1.8% to $90.28 per barrel following President Donald Trump's announcement of an agreement for Russian diesel supplies, easing some macroeconomic pressure on crypto markets.
title: Bitcoin Trades Near $84,000 Despite ETF Outflows, Oil Prices Slip

details: Bitcoin is currently trading around $83,044, with market participants keenly awaiting the release of the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) on October 14 and Producer Price Index (PPI) on October 15. These inflation reports are expected to significantly influence Federal Reserve rate decisions, which in turn will impact cryptocurrency prices. Elevated US Treasury yields and lingering geopolitical uncertainties continue to weigh on investor sentiment, despite a recent recovery in Bitcoin and Ethereum.
title: Investors Await US CPI and PPI Data Amid Geopolitical Uncertainty
